# Some AI graders skip up to 4 in 10 questions, and their scores don't show it

<p class="paper-subtitle"><em>We asked 25 AI models to grade the same 760 questions, and counted every question they skipped as a miss.</em></p>

Say you ask an AI to check one answer on a test, where we already know the correct grade, and it comes back with nothing. The usual score just leaves that question out and grades the AI on the ones it did answer. We gave 25 AI graders the same 760 questions and counted every skip as a miss. One model, DeepSeek V4 Flash, was right 99.8% of the time when it answered, but only 80.3% of the time across all 760. That gap is what this paper is about.

Counting skips as misses reshuffles the ranking. One judge drops from 99.8% to 80.3%. The same model scored 84.5% with one setup and 97.4% with another.

## What we found

1. The best grader got 99% right.
2. Some graders skipped up to 4 in 10 questions.
3. How you set a model up changes its score.
4. A grader that gave the same answer every time would score 50.3%.

Every question we used has one right answer, because that's the only way to grade the graders fairly. So the results tell you how these models do at that job. They don't tell you which AI company is best overall.

If you're picking an AI grader, ask two questions besides its score: how many questions did it actually answer, and what settings was it run with?

## Methods

We ran each model once per question with a fixed prompt and a 30 second timeout. We treated a missing answer as a wrong grade.

We measured how far apart two graders can look when the differences could be luck. We used the McNemar test for paired comparisons and Holm-corrected p-values to control for running 25 comparisons at once. We also report 95% CI intervals from a Wilson score interval. The gold labels come from an answer key or an automatic checker.

The baseline is a grader that always gives the same answer, which scores 50.3%. Coverage is the share of the 760 questions a grader answered. EXP-029 is the consolidated analysis run, and the figure numbers are regenerated by scripts/generate_benchmark_figures.py.
